Barbara Stöckl nimmt in Gesprächen mit großen Persönlichkeiten das Publikum mit auf eine persönliche Reise ins Spannungsfeld zwischen Geschichte und Zukunft, Resümee und Vision und Erfahrungsschatz und unbekümmertem Zukunftsglauben.

Drei außergewöhnliche Persönlichkeiten gewähren persönliche Einblicke in ihre enge Verbundenheit mit der österreichischen Hauptstadt. Ihre individuellen Lebenswege und prägenden Erfahrungen spiegeln das Lebensgefühl von Wien facettenreich wider.

Über Jahrhunderte war Walfang ein lukrativer Wirtschaftszweig. Heute riskieren Walretter für jedes einzelne Tier, wenn nötig ihr Leben. Vor knapp 50 Jahren veröffentlichte der US-Biologe Roger Payne eine Schallplatte mit den Gesängen von Buckelwalen.

Die Weihnachtsinsel ist nur ein kleiner Punkt im Indischen Ozean. Ihre paradiesische Kulisse ist die Bühne für ein besonderes Tier: bis zu einem Meter groß und an die 100 Jahre alt. Es knackt Kokosnüsse und zieht den Menschen das Essen vom Teller.

In den Tiefen der Meere lebt eine Gruppe von Tieren mit unglaublichen Fähigkeiten. Knochenlose Kreaturen, die Farbe und Form verändern können. Saugnäpfe machen sie zu effizienten Jägern: Tintenfische. Ihnen wird auf den Grund gegangen.

In den Weiten des Südpazifiks liegt die Republik Fidschi. Die meisten der 300 Fidschi-Inseln sind verwitterte Spitzen erloschener Vulkane. Der Film spürt dem Leben der Menschen auf Fidschi nach und führt in eine faszinierende Inselwelt im Südpazifik.

Die Geschichte Asiens begann im heutigen Sibirien. Hier fanden Wissenschaftler rund um den Baikalsee das älteste Gestein des Kontinents. Damals sammelten sich zunächst immer mehr Landmassen um Sibirien, vor allem an der Westseite. Bei einem gewaltigen Zusammenstoß mit Europa vereinten sich dann die beiden Kontinente und das Uralgebirge entstand. Dort, wo das Meer einst die Erdteile voneinander trennte, werden heute in zahlreichen Minen kostbare Bodenschätze abgebaut.

Entscheidend für die Entwicklung des asiatischen Kontinents waren die Kollision mit dem indischen Subkontinent und das Aufeinandertreffen mit der Pazifikplatte. Bei seiner rasanten Drift nach Norden kollidierte Indien mit Sibirien und drückte das tibetanische Plateau zusammen. Das führte zu Erdbeben und der Bildung riesiger Erdspalten. Nepal, China, insbesondere die chinesische Gebirgsregion Kunlun Shan, leiden noch heute unter den Folgen dieser Kontinentalbewegungen.

pr.t: Kirstie and Phil's Love It or List It
pr.d: Kirstie Allsopp and Phil Spencer meet the Lindleys from Ashtead, Surrey. Having built up his business empire from home, cybersecurity expert Bill has inadvertently taken over their detached bungalow, and retired civil servant Pippa has had enough. She dreams of moving to Kent, where they can be closer to family and the coast.

Cliff announces his raise at the post office. Woody and Sam want a raise, but the bar's takings have been declining for three months, risking closure. To increase takings, Sam and Woody raffle a Caribbean cruise, attracting many customers.

When Carla leans that she is going to become a grandmother, her world comes crashing down as she doesn't feel old enough to be called "grandma" by anyone. Seeing that Carla's depressed, Rebecca decides to throw a slumber party for her.
Doug arranges a reunion for his high school football team, but is angry when his championship-winning block is attributed to his team-mate Tom, who is now in a wheelchair.
Arthur moves upstairs because his cellar gets too cold in the winter. Doug doesn't like it and waits eagerly for warmer weather, but Arthur does not seem to want to move back.
Doug is appalled when he finds out Carrie frequently cheats at board games. She tries to get better, but maybe the reason behind her behaviour needs to be found out first.
Ray and Debra prepare Ally for her first play date and reflect on their own first meeting and kiss.

After a PTA meeting Debra makes a comment about a mother who had a breast enhancement and gets upset after seeing Ray's reaction. When Ray returns home from a trip, Debra has a "big" surprise for him.
Ray and Debra have an argument about their new can opener, and Marie, Frank and Robert can't help getting involved.
Frasier's new boss (Alan Tudyk) buys a condo in Frasier's building and then copies his interior design.

Frasier hires a butler who spoils everyone in the household and offers Frasier some sage advice to help him in his bid to join the snobbish opera board. Elsewhere, Daphne wonders aloud if she and Niles will ever be able to declare their love and is further demoralised when Mel shows up at Frasier's party, forcing Niles to play along as her dutiful husband.

Frasier begins to suspect his attractive new attorney is unfairly running up his bill, and hotshot lawyer Donny agrees to drop the suit when he falls in love with another woman he intends to marry, but Daphne might not be able to leave well enough alone.
Roz introduces Frasier to her new boyfriend, Luke, and the two men hit it off. When Roz and Luke break up, Frasier hides his continuing friendship with him while supporting Roz during her heartbreak.

Charlie is expecting someone for dinner - but so is Caroline.
Caroline's university reunion brings a visit from her old rival - who helps herself to whatever she fancies.

Debra and Ray are annoyed at the over-the-top affection which Robert and Amy are expressing towards each other. To make matters worse, Robert and Amy dole out some marriage advice to Ray, and give Debra a book on how to maintain a good relationship.
Debra persuades Ray to hire Gianni to do some DIY work in their kitchen, but they both soon regret it due to their friend's laziness.
After Amy invites her brother Peter to stay for dinner, he makes himself at home on the couch and never leaves.
Ray fakes a headache to get out of spending time with Marie and lies to her about it. This lie leads to a series of lies from Ray and Debra which leads to a huge mess.
Sabrina resents having to live by all her aunt rules, but when she suddenly becomes the rule enforcer, she starts to see things differently.
Sabrina's bratty cousin pays a visit and though appearing sweeter and more grown-up, she has an ulterior motive - to steal Harvey from Sabrina. Watch out Sabrina.
Sabrina's indecisiveness over which college place to accept causes her to be torn apart, literally, into four different Sabrinas.
Josh and Harvey are fighting for Sabrina's affection, so she feeds them magic friendship bread to bring peace, but they become too close and start to ignore her.
Chandler is aghast when Monica buys painfully expensive boots, and Phoebe tries to capitalise on her discovery that Ross's son attends school with the son of rock star Sting.
Ross's new girlfriend wants to put their photograph on Christmas cards, Rachel eyes Joey as a possible romantic partner, and the newlyweds cope with Chandler's boss as he goes through a divorce.
pr.sub: The One With Ross' Step Forward

pr.d: As Joey agonises over his secret affection for Rachel, Monica mistakenly thinks that he is infatuated with Phoebe. Meanwhile, Ross and Rachel promise not to try to find out the sex of their unborn child, but Rachel can't resist having a peek inside the doctor's confidential folder. Also, Monica urges a reluctant Chandler to enjoy the soothing pleasures of a scented bath, but realises that she's created a tub monster.
pr.sub: The One Where Chandler Takes a Bath

pr.d: Joey rushes pregnant Rachel to hospital when she experiences pains. When Ross feels left out, Joey makes a gallant suggestion. Meanwhile, Chandler is surprised to discover what is behind the locked door of Monica's secret cupboard, and Phoebe gets the impression that Monica is enjoying one of her massages a little too much.
pr.sub: The One With the Secret Closet

pr.d: Monica prepares for a sexy Valentine's Day, but Chandler is too shell-shocked after accidentally viewing Rachel's birthing video. Meanwhile, Phoebe gives Joey the world's most cheerful dog.
pr.sub: The One With the Birthing Video

pr.d: A guilt-ridden Joey finally confesses his love for Rachel to the flabbergasted Ross, while Chandler becomes nervous when Phoebe's handsome new boyfriend Don shares numerous personality traits with Monica.
pr.sub: The One Where Joey Tells Rachel

pr.d: In an effort to restore normality to their friendship, Rachel tells Joey a big lie about her unborn child. Meanwhile, Phoebe's tea leaves reveal that she will soon encounter the man of her dreams.
pr.sub: The One With the Tea Leaves

pr.d: Phoebe brings her irritatingly cheerful boyfriend to Mr and Mrs Geller's 35th anniversary party. Meanwhile, Ross is stunned when his parents ask him and the pregnant Rachel to feign marriage to avoid scandal.

Joey is thrilled when his name is used in a 'Soap Opera Digest' crossword puzzle. He is reluctant to let the magazine do a profile of him, but Rachel tries to persuade him to reconsider so that he can mention her.

Monica and Phoebe host Rachel's baby shower but forget to invite her mother. Rachel realises she is clueless about caring for the baby after birth. Meanwhile, Joey auditions to host a new game show called 'Bamboozled'.
pr.sub: The One With the Baby Shower

pr.d: When Monica's cooking at the restaurant receives a harsh write-up in a newspaper, she goes to a criticism class taught by the reviewer, hoping to convince him to reconsider his opinion. Meanwhile, Rachel gets upset when a cute salesgirl flirts with Ross while he and Rachel are shopping for baby supplies, and nervous about a major job interview, Chandler receives some questionable coaching from Phoebe.
pr.sub: The One With the Cooking Class

pr.d: Eight days overdue, Rachel grows irritable, prompting a bet between Monica and Phoebe. Meanwhile, Joey invites Chandler to his new film's screening.
pr.sub: The One Where Rachel Is Late

pr.d: Rachel waits in the hospital maternity ward with an anxious Ross. To her dismay, she is put in a semi-private room. Then, the heavily pregnant Janice is assigned to share the room with her.
pr.sub: The One Where Rachel Has a Baby

pr.d: Rachel doubts Ross's commitment to her and the baby. Meanwhile, Ross wants to confess his love for Rachel. Joey discovers Ross's mother's engagement ring on the floor.
pr.sub: The One Where Rachel Has a Baby

pr.d: Due to a misunderstanding, Rachel finds herself engaged to Joey instead of Ross shortly after giving birth to her and Ross's baby girl. Meanwhile, Joey can't help taking a look as Rachel tries unsuccessfully to nurse her baby. Inspired to have a baby of their own, Monica and Chandler retire to a hospital cupboard for a little privacy.
pr.sub: The One Where No One Proposes

pr.d: Joey's futile attempts to gain Ross's forgiveness for mistakenly asking Rachel to marry him only result in emergency hospitalisation. Meanwhile, an exhausted Rachel desperately searches for a solution to end baby Emma's non-stop crying.

Das neueste Experiment, Faultier, hat die Angewohnheit, aus tüchtigen Menschen Nichtstuer zu machen. Die Kinder aus der "Disneys Große Pause"-Serie sind zu Besuch und helfen Lilo, das Experiment einzufangen. Plötzlich merkt das superkluge Gretchen, dass ein hamsterartiger Satellit die Welt umkreist. Als Lilo das sieht, weiß sie, dass Dr. van Hamsterdam dahinter steckt. Sie will Faultiers Blitze ableiten, um Hamsterdams Satellit zu treffen und lahmzulegen.

Phineas und seine Freunde entgehen der Hitze, indem sie den größten Wassertropfen der Welt erschaffen, um darin zu plantschen. Unterdessen lässt Buford seinen Fisch am Danville Fischwettbewerb teilnehmen. Pinky und Perry arbeiten zusammen, um Dr. Doofenschmirtz daran zu hindern, die Besitzurkunde des Tristate-Gebietes aus dem Rathaus zu stehlen. Phineas und Ferb helfen der besorgten Isabella bei der Suche nach Pinky.

Mama erinnert sich an Bluey und Judo als Babys. Bluey war der erste, der rollen lernte, aber Judo war der erste, der krabbeln konnte, deswegen entstand schließlich ein Wettrennen, um zu sehen, welches Kind zuerst laufen kann.

Papa findet, dass seine Kinder viel zu viele Spielsachen haben und schlägt vor, sie wegzuwerfen. Um ihren geliebten Mr. Monkeyjocks zu retten, müssen Bluey und Bingo beweisen, dass das ihr Lieblingsspielzeug etwas Besonderes ist.

Als Dede unerwartet zu Besuch kommt, sprechen Mitch und Cam über die Rolle, die Mutter Pritchett in ihrem Leben spielt. Unterdessen warten Phil, Luke, Haley und Alex auf den richtigen Moment, um Claire schlechte Nachrichten zu überbringen.

Der geschiedene Scott bekommt am Weihnachtsabend Besuch von seinem Sohn Charlie. Als er ihn zu Bett bringen will, sehen sie Santa Claus vom Dach fallen. Dieser verschwindet zwar, doch seine Kleidung und eine Karte bleiben zurück. Auf der Karte steht, dass wer auch immer Santas Mantel nach dessen Tode trägt, zum neuen Santa wird. Scott und Charlie fahren daraufhin mit Santas Rentierschlitten zum Nordpol, wo der Weihnachtself Bernard Scott unterrichtet. So beginnt ein wundersames Abenteuer.

Bruce Nolan ist ein Boulevardfernsehreporter in Buffalo, New York, der mit fast allem in seinem Leben unzufrieden ist, trotz seiner Popularität und der Liebe seiner Freundin Grace. Am Ende des schlimmsten Tages in seinem Leben ist er wütend und lästert gegen Gott, und Gott reagiert. Er erscheint in menschlicher Form, stattet Bruce mit all seinen göttlichen Kräften aus, und fordert ihn auf, seinen Job zu übernehmen, um zu sehen, ob er ihn besser machen kann.

Jess versucht, sich mit Coach besser anzufreunden, und gibt vor, dasselbe Basketballteam wie er zu mögen. Nick allerdings verteidigt vehement sein Lieblingsteam und tritt deshalb in einen Sexstreik. Derweil tut sich für Winston eine neue Karriererichtung auf und Schmidt muss auf der Arbeit einen neuen Kollegen einarbeiten, der allerdings viel älter ist als er.

Gordon heads to Wilkinsburg, Pennsylvania, home to Ms Jean's Southern Cuisine, which was opened 12 years ago by retired special education teacher Ms Jean Gould. Her employees say she's like Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and that's why the local community stay away. Ms Jean insists she's only mean because her employees are lazy, but the business is falling apart.

This week, Gordon visits beachside restaurant Barefoot Bob's in Hull, Massachusetts, owned by husband-and-wife team Marc and Lisa. The duo opened the grill in the summer of 2004 to a busy seafront crowd, but every year the bottom line collapses through the bleak winter months.

pr.d: David and Natalie have each chosen their first keepers, but David can't get his mind off Natalie. She, however, seems pretty smitten with her keeper. Plus: condom mind games.
Self-professed 'crazy camel lady' Sandra wants a mature man to ride off into the sunset with. Pansexual erotic writer Toni-Ann dreams of being the heroine in her own sexy novel.
Three daters return to the restaurant hoping for better luck second time around, while some couples who had great dates return - and one of them gets down on bended knee...
The Goggleboxers have been watching The Crown, Survivor, 007: Road to a Million, The Good Ship Murder and Shoplifters: Caught Red Handed.
Brand new series - Alex: Jacob is shocked to find out that his colleagues aren't invested in his frequent email messages. Gregory turns to Janine for help with a former student.
Treehouse of Horror XXIV: In three spine-tingling stories, Homer rhymes in a Dr Seuss-style tale, Bart is beheaded in a kite-flying prang, and a travelling circus visits town.
Bottle Episode: Homer must transport a million-dollar bottle of wine to Mr Burns's mansion. And for once, it's not actually him who screws it up.
Spaceballs: Adam tries to start a Mel Brooks club after watching the movie Spaceballs. Erica plans to tell Beverly and Pops about a big decision she's made.
Let's Val Kilmer This Car: When Lainey turns down Barry's invitation to take her to the prom, he plans a prank with Principal Ball's car to get out of going.
Express Yourself: Phil has the crazy idea of going on a spontaneous trip to Paris with Claire. And Jay takes over their bathroom renovation.
Man Shouldn't Lie: Claire brings home a stray dog and gets the kids to help her hide it. And Cameron rents out the upstairs apartment to a Christian rock band.
Strangers in the Night: When Alex tells Phil and Claire she has a boyfriend, they worry that they've put too much pressure on her and that she's made up an imaginary boyfriend.
Haley's 21st Birthday: The family take Haley to a bar to celebrate her 21st birthday. Can Claire convince Haley to see her as a friend, rather than as her uptight mum?
A short, cheeky clip from Rude Tube's naughty little sister, Rude(ish) Tube, featuring sports of the lawnmower, motorbike and bicycle variety.
In Bournemouth, David and AJ plan a South African menu - with bread in every course. Vinnie and Alex serve South American dishes. And Andrea and Wayne's Vietnamese night doesn't go to plan.
Gordon Ramsay revisits three restaurants to find out if they've continued to follow his advice. How have Down City, Classic American and Davide fared in his absence?
Gordon Ramsay revisits four restaurants he tried to help: the Spanish Pavillion in New Jersey, and Kingston Café, La Frite and Capri in California.
The two series winners compete to win a cruise holiday. Plus: people unintentionally do the splits. And more. Alfonso Ribeiro hosts.
Banks Shot: When Will gets hustled in a pool hall and almost loses the family car, Uncle Phil comes to his rescue and outhustles the hustlers.
72 Hours: Carlton accepts Will's challenge to survive for two days in a tough LA neighbourhood.
The Bart Wants What It Wants: Rainier Wolfcastle's daughter (guest star Reese Witherspoon) develops a crush on Bart.
The Lastest Gun in the West: Bart befriends a cowboy who used to be a film star and tries to help him regain his fame. But he isn't prepared for his new hero's love of booze.
The Flandshees of Innersimpson: Flanders vows never to speak to Homer again after Homer steals his new headphones. Homer's absolutely delighted - at first...
Blame It on Lisa: The Simpsons go to Brazil to meet an orphan who Lisa has secretly been writing to. But as soon as they arrive, Homer is kidnapped.
Sixteen Candles: Murray and Beverly forget Adam's 16th birthday.
You Got Zuko'd: Adam's girlfriend Jackie returns from her summer in New York but acts like a different person. Beverly is unhappy with Lainey's culinary skills.
Double-Click: Claire can't seem to find the right time to fire an employee, Phil thinks he caught Luke with a girl in his bed, and no one notices that Alex has moved back.
A Tale of Three Cities: There's a reunion after trips took the Dunphys to New York; Mitch, Cam and Lily to the Midwest; and Jay, Gloria, Manny and Joe to Juarez in Mexico.
A Stereotypical Day: Jay goes out of his way to make a good impression on the new neighbours.
Blindsided: The Dunphys and Pritchetts go head-to-head when Luke decides his best chance of getting into college is to run against Manny in the senior class president election.
Yellow Subterfuge: Bart becomes a model student so that he can go on a school trip on a submarine. But Principal Skinner has other ideas...
White Christmas Blues: When radioactive steam from the nuclear power plant mixes with pollution, snow falls over Springfield and the town is inundated with holiday revellers.
Steal This Episode: Irked by high cinema ticket prices, Homer starts screening pirated movies in his back garden. But the FBI soon catch up with him...
Married to the Blob: Comic Book Guy asks Homer for advice on how to woo cute comic fan Kumiko, who visits his shop to research material for an autobiographical manga.
The Great Money Caper: When Homer leaves Bart by the squid port, kind strangers start giving money to the 'street urchin'. So Homer and Bart turn to a life of scamming.
Brand new series - 2 Ava 2 Fest: Ava Fest is back, and with the help of the teachers, Ava's determined to outdo last year by any means necessary.
The Big Four-Oh: When Vivian turns 40, she becomes obsessed with achieving her lifelong dream of being a professional dancer.
She Ain't Heavy: Will takes the shallow way out when his friends tease him about his date (guest star Queen Latifah).
What do Britain's top armchair critics think of Squid Game: The Challenge, The Couple Next Door, The Toy Hospital, Survivor, Vinnie Jones in the Country and Lorraine?
What do the Goggleboxers think of Squid Game: The Challenge, The Couple Next Door, Strictly Come Dancing, The Graham Norton Show, Planet Earth III, and Jingle All the Way?

pr.t: Mary Berry's Country House at Christmas
pr.d: When it comes to Christmas food and entertaining, Britain's country houses have always put on a show. Mary Berry visits Harewood House in Yorkshire to meet its army of skilled staff and dedicated volunteers as they prepare the house for Christmas. With its Robert Adam interiors, Chippendale furniture and Capability Brown gardens, Harewood is one of the nation's most beautiful stately homes.

Five merry cookie makers put their sweet spin on Christmas wreaths. Then, in a Christmas pull-me-up display challenge, the cookiers release a tsunami of icing that completely transforms their towering displays.

Five festive cookie makers use their imaginations to decorate cookies that feature the perfect present for ol' Saint Nick. The bakers also fashion the ultimate Christmas party-starter: life-size ugly Christmas jumpers.

Jesse Palmer welcomes the 12 bakers by challenging them to create autumn pavlova wreaths. The competitors divide into cake and pie teams to decide the best holiday dessert and win immunity from judges Nancy Fuller, Duff Goldman and Carla Hall.
Five teams of cake and sugar artists must imagine what happens outside the North Pole and make a creation symbolising Santa Claus as a world hero.

Divertida proposta en que dúas nais, con estilos de vida opostos, intercambiarán o seu fogar durante unha semana. Ao final da semana, as dúas familias enfróntanse para expoñer as súas diferenzas no seu modo de organizar a vivenda.

Un programa de entretemento onde, a modo de concurso, tres estranxeiros de tres nacionalidades distintas e que viven en tres localidades diferentes de Galicia terán que demostrar cal deles está máis integrado na nosa comunidade.

Cada semana daremos un paseo pola nosa terra visitando os lugares e veciños máis descoñecidos, os máis simpáticos, os máis característicos e os máis sorprendentes, uns destinatarios moi especiais que teñen moito que contar sobre Galicia.

Retrato de tres familias galegas que pertencen a distintos estratos sociais e residen en Santalla: os Cabana, labradores e propietarios dun ultramarinos, conviven cos Lamela, saga de caciques que ten contas pendentes cos Freire.

The two chefs who have made it through cook their four courses again. They are hoping to impress the formidable panel of judges, Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver, who are joined by tennis's greatest entertainer, Mansour Bahrami.

With finals week ahead of them, judge Andi Oliver first summons the chefs to 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon to have a look at where they could be cooking if they win. The judges are joined by guest judge Sue Barker, host of the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon coverage for more than 20 years.

The chefs must cook their fish courses but with some exceptionally high scoring dishes in the regional heats, each chef will need to deliver perfection in order to see off the competition. The judges are joined by guest judge Tim Henman.

It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all eight chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judge Gordon Reid.

It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British number one and Junior 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon champion.
It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.
The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.
The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

Young Cole Sear is haunted by a dark secret: he is visited by ghosts. Cole is frightened by visitations from those with unresolved problems who appear from the shadows. He is too afraid to tell anyone about his anguish, except child psychologist Dr Malcolm Crowe. As Dr Crowe tries to uncover the truth about Cole's supernatural abilities, the consequences for client and therapist are a jolt that awakens them both to something unexplainable.

pr.t: Find It, Fix It, Flog It
pr.d: Henry and Simon return to Norfolk to check out a farm full of junk. Henry immediately spots a stationary engine and a Fergie tractor while Simon finds a wheeled table.
Angus explores Boyzone star Shane Lynch's super-cars and a camper-van-turned-mini-bar. Then he checks out presenter Julia Bradbury's Victorian chair.
Brenda asks Angus to find new homes for her jewellery collection. But it's her son's childhood toys that might make big bucks on auction day.
There's breakdowns, brisk weather and a macabre discovery for Mark Hill and Margie Cooper as they travel from Darlington to Barnard Castle.
Angus travels to Scotland to meet Norma, a widow struggling to let go of her late husband's much-loved possessions as she prepares to downsize.
Actress Helen Flanagan asks Angus to sell some Corrie keepsakes and haute couture, while comedian Bobby Davro brings coins and sporting memorabilia.
Deep in the countryside, expert restorers take in Britain's broken and battered artefacts and bring them back to life while learning the rich history of the objects.
How do they run Ryker's Island, one of the biggest jails in the world? How do they make the famous Royal Mail post box? And how do they turn fruit into jam.
How do they make playing cards that can defeat a cheat? How do they brew a billion bottles of lager a year? And how do they make the world's most luxurious private jets.

pr.t: World War II: Saving the Reality
pr.d: Kenneth W Rendell's collection of World War II memorabilia features more than 6,000 original artefacts, including propaganda posters, French Resistance clothing, a Japanese admiral's uniform and a Sherman tank.
Technological innovations in U.S. naval aviation change the face of war.
Technological innovations in U.S. Navy aviation change the face of war.
The true story of two pilots, one American and the other Japanese, who confronted each other during a key WWII battle and, for some mysterious reason, did not shoot each other down.

pr.t: The Misty Experiment: The Secret Battle for the Ho Chi Minh Trail
pr.d: A look at the US Air Force squadron whose pilots volunteered to search for enemy supply transports and anti-aircraft installations concealed within the web of trail paths and waterways collectively known as the Ho Chi Minh Trail.

pr.t: Forbidden Knowledge: Forgotten Cities Lost in Time
pr.d: The filmmaker explores the lost underground cities of the ancient world.

pr.t: Ramesses The Great - Legendary Pharoah of Ancient Egypt
pr.d: Ramesses the Great, born in the 14th century BC, was part of Egypt's prosperous Bronze Age era.

Egyptologist Dr Chris Naunton explores the story of how Ancient Egypt was rediscovered, and how its historic sites and treasures were gradually decoded. A look into Egyptomania, the French invasion under Napoleon, and more.
Guernsey, the only British isle occupied by Nazi Germany during WWII, reveals unique wartime history.

Hungarian Jews Magda Brown and George Brent, who survived the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp as teenagers, reveal the human aspects of survival, resistance, chance, and luck in the face of Nazi tyranny.
No description available · EPGTalk.com

pr.t: World War II: Saving the Reality
pr.d: Kenneth W Rendell's collection of World War II memorabilia features more than 6,000 original artefacts, including propaganda posters, French Resistance clothing, a Japanese admiral's uniform and a Sherman tank.

In the run-up to September 1939, political and economic chaos in the aftermath of World War I allowed Hitler in Germany, Mussolini in Italy and ultranationalists in imperial Japan to seize absolute power.

Germany took just four weeks to conquer Poland, using a new form of warfare, Blitzkrieg. Six armoured tank units known as Panzer divisions, supported by the Luftwaffe, quickly broke through Polish defences.

After the retreat from Dunkirk, Churchill rallied Britain in its darkest hour. Hitler was only just across the channel, but he reckoned without our supreme strategist, the might of the navy and the manoeuvrability of the air force.
Explores Hitler's assault on the Soviet Union in the summer of 1941.
The attack on Pearl Harbour brought the country nicknamed the 'sleeping giant', aka America, into the war, and saw the emergence of the aircraft carrier as the pre-eminent weapon of the seas.

Italian dictator Benito Mussolini dreamed of recreating the Roman Empire and making the Mediterranean the centre of a new vast colonial empire, including British-controlled Egypt and Sudan to the south.

With their armies fully engaged on the battlegrounds, the Allied and Axis powers focused their efforts to develop new weapons and new strategies to deliver a knockout blow to the enemy and bring about a quick end to the conflict.
After Hitler's gamble in the East fails, the Soviet Union starts to slowly push back and grow.

By early 1944, Hitler had long been expecting an Allied attack on north-western France, but his problem was knowing when and where it would come. This episode has a look at the Allied operations Bodyguard and Overlord.
Concentrates on Hitler's attempts to shift the balance of power back in his favour.
The war in the Pacific against Japan was a savage hand-to-hand, island-to-island struggle, fought by new specialist fighting units like the valiant Chindits.
Allied forces converge on Germany, uncovering the horrors of Belsen and Buchenwald, before pushing towards Berlin, where Adolf Hitler is clinging to power in his last desperate days.

In the run-up to September 1939, political and economic chaos in the aftermath of World War I allowed Hitler in Germany, Mussolini in Italy and ultranationalists in imperial Japan to seize absolute power.
Discovering the truth of the unsolved murder of Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll, who was shot in Kenya in 1941, and why the only suspect was acquitted.
pr.sub: The Earl of Erroll: Death in the Valley

pr.d: Tsar Nicholas II and his family were killed by Bolsheviks in July 1918, but an incredible theory suggests that daughter Anastasia survived.
Adam, Kru and Tony follow the path of a failed 1982 Vancouver news team led by a Slumach gold hunter and mystic dowser.
After aborting his mission last season, lone wolf prospector David Muise returns undeterred and looking for a partner.

Professor Alice Roberts explores British history through the stories of individual towns. Alice examines Britain in wartime by looking at the coastal town of Dover, a town that found itself on the frontline in the struggle against Nazi Germany.
Professor Alice Roberts explores the Georgian era in her hometown of Bristol, from architectural gems to the world's first chocolate factory, backstreet gin and the horror of the slave trade.
Andy visits Hereford Cathedral to discover the cider tax's role in the American Civil War, while Jayne explores local legends, including a bell stealing mermaid and a girl's love for her pet dragon.
Alice Roberts explores the story of Stewart Britain by visiting Stirling, the home of the Scottish royals who eventually took the English throne in 1603 and created Great Britain.
Alice investigates what life was like in pre-Roman Britain. Relying on archaeology, she examines the two Hebridean Bronze Age skeletons known as the Cladh Hallan mummies.

Dr Alice Roberts goes in search of our elusive Stone Age ancestors. Along the way she visits the Channel island of Jersey where she meets a team of archaeologists hoping to shed new light on the much-maligned Neanderthals, and embarks on a kayak survey of the coastline looking for undiscovered sites hidden in the cliffs. At the Natural history museum Alice sees the dark side of our Ice Age ancestors lives.

Colourisation of historic film creates a vivid portrait of the Royal Family from the late 19th century onwards. Includes the earliest film of Queen Victoria, and Edward and Wallis Simpson marrying in exile.
Colourised film creates a vivid portrait of the British Empire from its peak in the early 20th century through uprisings, wars and inevitable decline. Includes early colour home movies from the Raj.
Alice enjoys a Roman feast in Britain's most Roman city, Chester. She examines a radical theory on the Romans' plans for the city and explores an incredible archaeological find deep underground.
In York, Professor Alice Roberts takes part in a Viking battle, meets the metal detectorists behind one of the UK's greatest archaeological finds, and gets her hands on Viking poo.

Andy McGrath joins Dr Kate Cherrell to explore the legends of the Kidsgrove boggart and a haunted canal. He seeks the lair of Sir Gawain's enemy, the Green Knight, while uncovering tales of werewolves, black-eyed children and trolls in Cannock Chase.
Andy explores Edinburgh's haunted vaults, traces the steps of Burke and Hare, visits the Culloden battlefield, and seeks the legend of a Scottish hero in a hidden cave.

Finds include: revelations from 'Britain's Pompeii', the 3,000-year-old perfectly preserved village in Cambridgeshire, including how Bronze Age ancestors designed their homes, and their kitchens packed with food and equipment, and the theatre where Shakespeare premiered Romeo and Juliet and Henry V.

A look at the camp from which Vikings invaded Britain, and groundbreaking evidence that the world-famous Avebury stone circle isn't just a sacred site but a place where people lived and worked. In Staffordshire, the oldest Iron Age gold in Britain is unearthed.
pr.sub: Viking Camp And Iron Age Gold

pr.d: With the aid of dramatic reconstruction, Dan Jones explores the 900-year history of the beautiful Leeds Castle in Kent, from its origins as a royal Saxon family's manor and Norman stronghold to the private property of six medieval queens, a Tudor palace, a Jacobean country house, a Georgian mansion and an elegant 20th-century retreat for the rich and famous.

In medieval England, the North was ruled from York. Dan Jones explores the history of its castle, from the Viking Jorvik and the Normans, through the dark days of the anti-Jewish pogrom and the imprisonment of the Knights Templar, to one of its most colourful inmates - the legendary highwayman Dick Turpin.

Alice visits Canterbury for the story of Plantagenet England. Canterbury is steeped in history and the era of the Plantagenets - the strong house that held the English throne from 1154 until 1485 - saw the most dramatic episodes in the city's story.
Alice Roberts explores the story of Stewart Britain by visiting Stirling, the home of the Scottish royals who eventually took the English throne in 1603 and created Great Britain.

Colourized rare archival film and home movies brings Churchill back to life. Includes moments of drama, alongside playful scenes with Charlie Chaplin and Churchill losing his shorts in his swimming pool.

Colourisation of historic film creates a vivid portrait of the Royal Family from the late 19th century onwards. Includes the earliest film of Queen Victoria, and Edward and Wallis Simpson marrying in exile.
Before the Unabomber, New Yorkers were terrified for 16 years by an attacker who planted bombs across the city. The culprit was an electrician named George Metesky.
The strange story of Michael Malloy shows how some people just won't die when you want them to.

Cindy Crawford bittet Jonathan und Drew um Hilfe, um ihre beste Freundin und Trainerin zu überraschen. Nach vielen Herausforderungen in deren Leben möchte Cindy mit einer glamourösen Hausrenovierung ein besonderes Dankeschön ausdrücken.

Weil der Schauspieler Rob Lowe einer engen Freundin seine Dankbarkeit zeigen will, will er gemeinsam mit Jonathan und Drew ihr Zuhause renovieren. Sowohl die Küche als auch der Wohnbereich sollen modernisiert und funktional umgestaltet werden.
Nach dem tragischen Verlust ihres Sohnes und Bruders möchten Mutter und Tochter gemeinsam einen Neuanfang wagen. Mit dem Erlös aus seinem Nachlass suchen sie in Ojai, Kalifornien, ein Zuhause.
Aus ehemaligen Reinigungskräften sind erfolgreiche Unternehmer geworden, die heute ein florierendes Reinigungsunternehmen führen.

Ein New Yorker Pärchen gewinnt ganze sieben Millionen US-Dollar in einer Lotterie. Aus diesem Grund wollen sie nun in den Ruhestand in Vero Beach gehen. Der Immobilienfachmann namens David Bromstad soll die passende Bleibe finden.

Ein alleinerziehender Vater gewinnt dort eine Million US-Dollar in einer Lotterie. Da er von Beruf Anwalt ist, wird er seinem dreijährigen Sohn ohnehin kein schlechtes Leben bieten. Nun soll jedoch eine pompöse Immobilie erworben werden.

Ein pensionierter Feuerwehrmann gewinnt eine stattliche Summe in einer Lotterie. Aus diesem Grund möchte er sich eine beeindruckende Liegenschaft zulegen. Der Immobilienfachmann namens David Bromstad soll diese beschaffen.

Der Immobilienfachmann macht sich mit Neureichen auf die Suche nach der passenden Immobilie. Der Zuschauer erhält Einblicke in den Beschaffungsprozess von ansehnlichen Liegenschaften. Darüber hinaus wird einiges an Euphorie gezeigt.

In der Hoffnung, finanziell unabhängiger zu werden, verlässt Lisa Colorado und zieht nach Austin, Texas, um in einem Minihaus ein neues Leben zu beginnen. Mithilfe ihrer besten Freundin Tara sucht sie nach einem mobilen Cottage, für das sie einen Stellplatz mieten will, bevor sie Land kaufen kann. Aber mit einem Budget von 50.000 Dollar und einer umfassenden Wunschliste wird es für Lisa schwer werden, ein passendes Minihaus zu finden.

Jeffrey, Student in Wisconsin, lebte auf engstem Raum in Südkorea, wo er eine Zeit lang als Englischlehrer arbeitete. Jetzt möchte er sein Zuhause auch in Wisconsin verkleinern. Er hofft, nach seinem Abschluss eine Arbeit in einem Nationalpark zu finden, und wünscht sich deshalb ein mobiles Haus. Mit seiner Mutter Joan ist er auf der Suche nach einem Haus, das weniger als 28 Quadratmeter bietet.

Die Architekturstudentin Stephanie will von zu Hause ausziehen. Sie baut sich ein Minihaus, über das sie ihre Abschlussarbeit an der Hochschule in St. Petersburg, Florida, schreibt. Ihr Vater Joe hat Stephanie angeboten, ihr beim Bau zu helfen. Sie besichtigen Musterhäuser, die Stephanie ihren Ansprüchen entsprechend modifizieren könnte. Mit einem Budget von 20.000 Dollar wünscht sie sich ein Haus in rustikalem Ambiente mit einem Oberlicht im Schlafzimmer.

Andrew und Raquel reisen von Delray Beach, Florida, nach Memphis, Tennessee, um sich mit einem Bauunternehmer zu treffen, der ihnen ein bewegliches kleines Haus in ihrer Heimatstadt bauen kann, das sie überall hin mitnehmen können. Raquel bevorzugt ein Haus im Cottage-Stil mit viel Platz zum Atmen, während Andrew etwas möchte, das so klein wie möglich ist und Details im Industrie-Design aufweist. Die beiden haben ein Budget von 55.000 Dollar.

Aubree und Jordan hoffen, im teuren Los Angeles, Kalifornien, ein Minihaus zu finden, das sie nach ihren Wünschen gestalten können. Sie suchen nach einem renovierungsbedürftigen Haus mit Fundament und genügend großem Grundstück für ihre Tiere. Jordan will ein Minihaus, das nur weniger Restaurierungen bedarf. Aubree dagegen ist bereit zu einer Komplettrenovierung. Mit einem Budget von nur 265.000 Dollar ist es in L.A. schwer, etwas zu finden.

Paige überredet ihren skeptischen Freund Pierre zu einer Motorradtour durch Vietnam. Als ihnen das Geld ausgeht, nimmt Paige einen Lehrerjob in Hoi An an. Aber bei der Suche nach einer Unterkunft treten erneut verschiedene Ansichten zutage.

Um das Leben als Unternehmer hinter sich zu lassen, zieht ein Paar mit seinen zwei Kindern von Seattle nach Costa Rica. Bei der Suche nach einem neuen Zuhause treten allerdings die unterschiedlichen Vorstellungen zutage.

Die Taucher Craig und Heather möchten ihr sicheres Leben aufgeben und als digitale Nomaden an der mexikanischen Riviera Maya leben. Doch die idyllische Region ist groß und so ist auch das Angebot an Plätzen für das neue Zuhause.
pr.sub: Von Florida auf die grüne Insel

pr.d: Zwei Akademiker möchten von San Diego nach Frankreich ziehen. Aber während einem ein Dorfleben mit kleinen Gassen, Märkten und frischem Essen vorschwebt, hat der andere eine ganz andere Vorstellung vom neuen gemeinsamen Zuhause.

Jen und Rick ziehen von Pennsylvania nach Playa del Carmen, Mexiko. Ihnen schwebt ein zügiger Umzug vor. Als sie aber mit ihren sechs Koffern und ihrer Katze in ihrem neuen Zuhause ankommen, warten ungeahnte Überraschungen auf sie.
Diese Sendung wirbt für verschiedene Produkte, die man sich bequem nach Hause schicken lassen kann.

Jeff, dessen Eltern sieben Millionen Dollar gewonnen und mit ihm und seinem Bruder geteilt haben, will seine Strandbude gegen ein Haus im Ranch-Stil eintauschen. Er wünscht sich viel Platz, ein Schwimmbad und eine Lage in der Nähe des Flughafens.
Rave, Michelle und ihre beiden Kinder wohnen bei seinen Eltern, während sie ein Zuhause suchen.
Stephanie und Marc sind frustriert und wurden bei vielen ihrer Traumimmobilien überboten.

Das junge Paar Missy und Devon sucht nach einem Schnäppchen in Ormond-by-the-Sea, einem kleinen Badeort an der Ostküste Floridas. Gleichzeitig planen sie ihre Hochzeit. Sie finden ein Haus mit Beach-Feeling, das sie selbst renovieren wollen.
pr.sub: Ein Haus für die gemeinsame Zukunft

pr.d: Brian und Michelle suchen in Texas nach einem erschwinglichen Haus für ihre Familie, um näher bei Verwandten zu sein. Die Liste ihrer Renovierungswünsche ist lang, doch sie sind sich nicht sicher, ob ihr Budget ausreicht.

Eine Familie sucht nach einem neuen renovierungsbedürftigen Traumhaus in der Nähe vom Strand von New Jersey, da sie viele positive Erinnerungen an den Ort hat. Da das Budget knapp ist und die Wunschliste lang, gibt es immer wieder Probleme.

Tamara und ihr Vater helfen einem Investor bei der Bewältigung zahlreicher Herausforderungen, indem sie eine Festung aus Stein und Beton umgestalten, um sie modern und vermietbar zu machen. Sie verwandeln die Betonburg in modernes Mietgold.

Tamara arbeitet mit einem Investor zusammen, um ein baufälliges Haus aus dem Jahr 1910 in eine Zufluchtsstätte in der Innenstadt zu verwandeln. Die Immobilie muss von oben bis unten entkernt werden. Das fertige Produkt ist eine marktreife Luxusmiete.

Ein junges Paar findet sein Traumhaus auf einem Golfplatz, aber das veraltete Design ist weit von ihren Träumen entfernt. Tamara und ihr Team retten den Tag, indem sie die Villa mit einem Hole-in-One-Design komplett renovieren.

Die Einrichtungsexpertin Kanoa Lloyd und ihr Team zeigen, wie man Ordnung in den Alltag bringt. Gemeinsam mit dem Schreiner Sean Brown und der Organisationsexpertin Natalie Jane entrümpeln sie chaotische Häuser in Neuseeland.

Die Einrichtungsexpertin Kanoa Lloyd und ihr Team zeigen, wie man Ordnung in den Alltag bringt. Gemeinsam mit dem Schreiner Sean Brown und der Organisationsexpertin Natalie Jane entrümpeln sie chaotische Häuser in Neuseeland.

Jack beginnt seine Reise in Nebraska und besichtigt ein aufwendig renoviertes Raketensilo. Danach besucht er ein märchenhaftes Cottage mit Hollywood-Vergangenheit und entdeckt zum Abschluss in Las Vegas ein außergewöhnliches Paradies für Autofans.

Jack besichtigt in Palm Springs das ehemalige Zuhause einer Hollywood-Legende. Dann reist er ins Goldgräberland und entdeckt eine ungewöhnliche Lösung für Stauraum, bevor es an den Lake Tahoe geht, wo nachhaltiges Bauen im Mittelpunkt steht.

Jacks Reise führt ihn zu drei weiteren außergewöhnlichen Häusern. Er entdeckt ein Haus mit musikalischer Inspiration, besucht eine Siedlung aus Erdkuppelbauten in der Wüste und wirft schließlich einen Blick in ein Anwesen mit königlichem Flair.

Jack besichtigt eine Kirche, die zu einem Wohnhaus umgebaut wurde. Danach besucht er ein farbenfrohes Haus in der kalifornischen Wüste und entdeckt schließlich ein historisches Gebäude, das eine völlig neue Bestimmung als Zuhause gefunden hat.

Im mittleren Westen tourt Retta durch drei abscheuliche Häuser, die um die Chance auf eine Renovierung wetteifern. Sie erhält einen Einblick in einen Unterwasser-Seepalast, einen Rückfall aus den 1960er-Jahren und ein ehemaliges Bestattungsinstitut.

Retta ist in den Südosten unterwegs, um sich die hässliche Heimkonkurrenz anzusehen. Retta erkundet ein Sardinenbüchsenhaus mit einem Schlangenproblem, ein Anwesen mit einer fragwürdigen Vergangenheit und ein Haus, das wie eine alte Bank aussieht.

Retta begibt sich in den Nordosten, um die abscheulichste Heimat der Region aufzudecken. Sie stellt das Leben infrage und entwirft Entscheidungen in einer ehemaligen Vorschule, einem Haus in Pyramidenform und einem Albtraum mit rosa Teppich.

Retta findet einen dunklen Fleck an der sonnigen Westküste, als sie drei Häuser untersucht, die eher Albträumen als Träumen ähneln. Sie besucht ein Dschungelhaus, ein Haus, das früher eine Scheune war und ein Boot ähnliches Anwesen.

Greg hat kaum Geld und schläft auf dem Sofa eines Freundes - bis er mit einem Rubbellos eine Million Dollar gewinnt. Davon möchte er maximal 200.000 Dollar in sein Traumhaus investieren, das ein großes Grundstück und vier Schlafzimmer haben soll.

Der alleinerziehende Vater Todd investiert spontan 10 Dollar in einen Lottoautomaten. Kurz darauf erfährt er, dass er 700.000 Dollar gewonnen hat. Todd will direkt aus seiner kleinen Mietwohnung in Louisville, Kentucky, in ein Eigenheim ziehen.

Martin is impressed with the potential of two shops and three flats in Tonypandy in Wales while Dion looks round a two-bedroom maisonette in Dawley and Lucy meets a first-time developer with ambitious plans for an end terrace in London's Forest Gate.
A first-floor one-bedroom flat in London's Stepney Green, a three-bed semi in Dartford in Kent and a one-bedroom flat on the 17th floor of a block in Salford are all sold under the hammer.

A 1930s bungalow in Dereham in Norfolk, a first-floor flat in London's East Ham and a property in Maryport in Cumbria with a hidden room are all sold at auction. Martin, Lucy and Dion meet the new owners and hear their plans for their investments.

For two of the properties sold under the hammer, a semi in Ilkeston in Derby and a flat in Streatham Hill in London, it's all about creating smart kitchens and bathrooms. Meanwhile, the owners of a bungalow have to deal with an unexpected issue.

A fifth-floor flat in Greater Manchester, a three-bed semi in Carlisle and three commercial buildings near Stansted are all sold under the hammer. One developer has a pressing deadline to finish his renovation work.

An old Derbyshire farmhouse in Wirksworth gets a stunning makeover, a developer builds a pair of semis in Chatham in Kent, while a mid-terraced house in Blackhall Colliery in County Durham is given a makeover ready for the rental market.

Martin, Lucy and Dion meet father-and-daughter developers. An apartment in a former mill in Mow Cop on the Staffordshire and Cheshire border, a three-bed semi in East Ham and a flat in Bournemouth are all given makeovers with the help of dad.

A couple about to get married buy their first home in Newcastle, a new dad thinks developing a flat in Leyton in London will give him more time with his four-month-old son, and a former IT worker develops a property in Gainsborough in Lincolnshire.
A flat over two floors in London's Camberwell, another flat in Telford in Shropshire and a three-bed semi in Alvaston in Derby are all sold under the hammer.
Martin, Lucy and Dion visit a grand five-bedroom period house in Folkestone in Kent, a two-bedroom flat in London's Leytonstone and a two-bedroom mid-terrace in Fenton in Stoke-on-Trent.

A studio flat in a former 1960s office block which is grade two listed in London's Elephant and Castle, a terraced house in Pontygwaith in South Wales and a flat in Cradley Heath near Birmingham are all sold under the hammer.
A house with no floor in Edgbaston in Birmingham, a detached house on several levels in Oldham and a former garage complex ripe for development in Forest Hill in London are all sold under the hammer.
A converted 16th-century chapel in Matlock in Derbyshire, a two-bedroom flat in Whetstone in London and a water-damaged house in Wishaw in Scotland are all sold under the hammer.

A two-bed semi in Meir in Stoke-on-Trent is given a country house look, a flat in London's Willesden Green also gets the wow factor, and a semi in Dudley in the West Midlands loses its 1980s look to be brought into the 21st century.
Terraced houses in Gravesend in Kent and Shipley in Derbyshire are given a new lease of life while former church premises in Harrow Weald in Middlesex are given a new use for the community.

Martin, Lucy and Dion meet property developers who have all bought at auction and hope to make a profit on their investments. Today a landscape gardener tackles a terrace in Ilkeston in Derby, two friends take on a four-storey house in Sittingbourne in Kent while another couple of friends' first venture together is a studio flat in South Norwood in London.

Dion visits a stone cottage in Tilton on the Hill in rural Leicestershire, Martin is at a property auction in Croydon on the outskirts of London, and Lucy meets two friends who have bought a bungalow in Rainham in Kent.

A mid-terrace house in Chaddesden in Derby, a two-bedroom flat in London's Maida Vale and a property in Warrington are all sold under the hammer. Martin Roberts, Lucy Alexander and Dion Dublin meet the new owners to hear what they have planned for their auction buys.

Martin looks round a pretty cottage with outbuildings with huge potential in Burton upon Trent, while Lucy checks out a flat in London's ⚽ [EPL] Crystal Palace and Dion is in Mossley near Manchester in a four-bedroom bungalow.

Martin tackles the issue of solar panels on a property in Mountain Ash in Wales and wonders if it will be a sunny outcome for the new owner, while Lucy looks round a barn in Elstree in Hertfordshire and Dion visits a flat in Newport in Shropshire.

Martin Roberts meets a couple who buy a former mill workers' cottage in Derbyshire as their first home together, Lucy Alexander meets a father and daughter team who are seasoned developers buying a house in Kent, and Dion Dublin talks to a man who, along with two friends, has clubbed together to buy an investment property in Lowestoft in Suffolk.

Dion Dublin is in Walsall in the Midlands looking around a 1950s semi, Martin Roberts meets a man developing a ground-floor one-bedroom flat in Ilford in Essex, and Lucy Alexander catches up on a multimillion-pound redevelopment.

pr.d: Das Campen begann als authentischer Natururlaub und wurde Jahre später zum extravaganten Luxustourismus. Anstatt das Notwendigste mit sich zu tragen, geht nun das voll möblierte Heim mit auf Reisen. Wer sind die Besitzer dieser teuren Wohnmobile?

In dieser Sendung geht es um die gigantische Betonkonstruktion der neuen Samuel-De-Champlain-Brücke, die über dem Sankt-Lorenz-Strom im kanadischen Quebec gebaut wurde. Täglich passieren tausende Fahrzeuge auf dieser Doppelschrägseilbrücke.

Wer würde sich nicht gerne mal wie ein Superheld fühlen? Mit dem Jetsuit eines britischen Unternehmens kann man sich mühelos in die Lüfte erheben und über den Himmel jagen. Der Harvesterkopf einer finnischen Firma fällt und entastet einen Baum binnen Sekunden und unterstützt obendrein eine verantwortungsvolle Forstwirtschaft. Und ein 3D-Drucker aus Dänemark erschafft auf Knopfdruck perfekt designte Häuser aus schnelltrocknendem Beton in fast jeder gewünschten Form.

Die Dokumentationen zeigt die Fortentwicklung der Transportmittel im Zuge der Globalisierung. Die Entwicklung von leistungsstarken Frachtflugzeugen, Hochseekolossen und Elektrozügen prägt die Zukunft des Güterverkehrs.

Am Flughafen von Santiago de Chile gerät die Anti-Drogen-Brigade in Alarmbereitschaft: Drei Touristen ohne Gepäck entpuppen sich nach einer Röntgenuntersuchung als Teil einer riskanten Schmuggeloperation. Zeitgleich sorgt eine Familie aus Hongkong für Aufsehen, als Unstimmigkeiten in ihren Pässen entdeckt werden. Und ein aus den USA abgeschobener Chilene gibt den Behörden Rätsel auf - was wird die Kontrolle ans Licht bringen?

Eine Gruppe von Landarbeitern trifft zur Erntezeit ein, doch einer von ihnen hat eine ganz andere Vorstellung davon, wie man Geld verdienen kann. Ein Actionfiguren-Sammler kehrt aus den Vereinigten Staaten zurück, mit Koffern voller Spielzeug.

Mehrere Männer erreichen die Grenze im Norden und geben an, nach Arbeit zu suchen. Doch fördert eine Untersuchung ihres Gepäcks einige seltsame Funde zutage. Ein junger Mann verlässt die USA, die Datenbanken enthüllen eine kriminelle Vergangenheit.

Am Flughafen von Santiago de Chile läuft die Arbeit der Zollbeamten auf Hochtouren: In einem Paket voller Fahrradstoßdämpfer entdecken sie mithilfe des Röntgenscanners verdächtiges organisches Material. Zudem gibts einen Diebstahl im Duty Free Shop.

pr.d: Craig und Sarah nehmen sich den noch immer ungeklärten Fall der "Phoenix-Lichter" vor.

Craig und Sarah befassen sich mit dem Fall von Chicago O'Hare, einer Massensichtung einer fliegenden Untertasse, die über einer United Airlines-Maschine schwebte. Der Vorfall wurde von mehreren Luftfahrtexperten, Piloten und Passagieren beobachtet.

Es wird über die NASA-Sonde "Osiris Rex", die einen für die Erde potenziell tödlichen Asteroiden abfangen und genau erforschen soll, berichtet. Die beeindruckenden Steine ermöglichen es, viel über dessen Vergangenheit und Zukunft lernen zu können.

Im September 2008 ist eine Boeing 737 der russischen Airline Aeroflot von Moskau auf dem Weg in die zentral russische Stadt Perm. Während des ganzen Fluges laufen die beiden Triebwerke mit unterschiedlicher Leistung. Der Erste Offizier muss permanent gegensteuern, um die Maschine auf Kurs zu halten. An Bord sind 82 Passagiere. Beim Anflug auf Perm stürzt die Maschine nahe der Stadt ab auf die Gleise der Transsibirischen Eisenbahn. Was führt zu der Katastrophe?

Über der sturmgepeitschten Nordsee wird eine Turboprop-Maschine vom Blitz getroffen. Im Cockpit fallen die Instrumente aus, das Flugzeug rast in die Tiefe, der Aufprall scheint unausweichlich. Bei der Untersuchung wird etwas Ungewöhnliches entdeckt.

Ein Privatjet befindet sich im Anflug auf den Flughafen von Akron im US-Bundesstaat Ohio. Kurz vor dem Ziel kommt es zur Katastrophe: Die Maschine knallt in ein Apartmentgebäude, alle Insassen sterben. Die Ermittler untersuchen, wie es dazu kam.
